examples.question_text: A rectangular garden measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm on a plan drawn to a scale of $1:400$. Find its actual area, in square metres.
examples.solution_text:
Use image : original for each length.
$\begin{aligned}\text{length}&=5\times400\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=3\times400\\&=1200\text{ cm}\\&=12\text{ m}\\A&=20\times12\\&=240\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A rectangular courtyard measures $6$ cm by $4$ cm on a plan drawn to a scale of $1:150$. Find its actual perimeter, in metres.
A floor plan gives measurements in millimetres. A rectangular room measures $5400$ mm by $3200$ mm. Find its floor area, in square metres.
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar $2$ cm long represents $80$ m. A rectangular field measures $4.2$ cm by $2.5$ cm on the photograph. Find its actual area, in square metres.
examples.solution_text:
Convert the scale-bar lengths to the same unit.
$\begin{aligned}80\text{ m}&=8000\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=2:8000\\&=1:4000\\\text{length}&=4.2\times4000\\&=16\,800\text{ cm}\\&=168\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=2.5\times4000\\&=10\,000\text{ cm}\\&=100\text{ m}\\A&=168\times100\\&=16\,800\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: On a floor plan, a scale bar $2$ cm long represents $1$ m. A rectangular kitchen measures $7$ cm by $5$ cm on the plan. Find its actual perimeter, in metres.
examples.solution_text: $\begin{aligned}1\text{ m}&=100\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=2:100\\&=1:50\\\text{length}&=7\times50\\&=350\text{ cm}\\&=3.5\text{ m}\\\text{width}&=5\times50\\&=250\text{ cm}\\&=2.5\text{ m}\\P&=2(3.5+2.5)\\&=12\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A rectangular swimming pool is $48$ m long. On a scale diagram it measures $3$ cm long and $1.25$ cm wide. Find its actual area, in square metres.
examples.solution_text:
Use the known length to find the scale, then convert the width.
$\begin{aligned}48\text{ m}&=4800\text{ cm}\\\text{image : original}&=3:4800\\&=1:1600\\\text{width}&=1.25\times1600\\&=2000\text{ cm}\\&=20\text{ m}\\A&=48\times20\\&=960\text{ m}^{2}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored seven worked examples covering all distinct assessed methods, with different values from the supplied source and assessments. Questions and solutions remain separate and editable; solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. The composite example includes an unshaded black diagram and solution-only decomposition annotations. Independent equations align at their relation signs; no bare-expression continuation requires a phantom gutter. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither changed nor re-audited. Final-size rendering and label verification remain for the later visual stage.

examples.derivation: The enclosing rectangle is 10 m by 6 m; the missing rectangle is 2 m by 3 m. Area = 60 − 6 = 54 m². Question coordinates agree with all dimensions. Solution dashed edges complete the enclosing rectangle without revealing working in the question.
80 m = 8000 cm, so image : original = 2 : 8000 = 1 : 4000. Real dimensions are 168 m and 100 m. Area = 16,800 m².
1 m = 100 cm, so image : original = 2 : 100 = 1 : 50. Real dimensions are 3.5 m and 2.5 m. Perimeter = 2(3.5 + 2.5) = 12 m.
